To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chlorinated benzoates, phenols, and benzenes enhance the rate and the extent of PCB dehalogenation, but the extent and the pattern of dechlorination enhancement varied depending on the type of chlorinated benzoate, phenol, or benzene.

chlorinated aromatic compounds, such as chlorobenzoate, chlorophenol, or chlorobenzene, enhanced polychlorinated-biphenyl dechlorination in sediments by enriching the dechlorinating microbial community.

the addition of chlorobenzenoates, chlorophenois and chlorobenzois to PCB-contaminated sediments can significantly enhance PCB dechlorination, and that different dechlorination patterns are induced depending on the type of HACs added.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of PCB dechlorinating microbial ecology, namely the effect of HACs on the enrichment and activity of PCB-dechlorination microorganisms.
the effects of haloaromatic compounds on PCB dechlorination and enrichment of PCB-dehalogenating bacteria.
the enhancement of PCB-dechlorination by chloroaromatic compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enhancement of PCB dechlorinating activity was related to the enrichment of the dechlorinators, which in turn was related to the number and types of dechlorinating microorganism(s) selected.
the addition of chlorobenzenoates, chlorophenois and chlorobenzoens to the PCB-contaminated sediments enhanced the extent of PCB dehalogenation by enriching PCB-dechlorinating microbes.
the enhancement of PCB dechlorinating activity was related to the enrichment of dechlorinating micro-organisms by HACs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the addition of haloaromatics to PCB-containing sediments enhanced the overall extent of dechlorinations, but the patterns of dechlorination were dependent on the type of haloaromatic compounds added.

chlorobenzoate-, chlorophenol- and chlorobenzene-amended sediments can be used for the enrichment of PCB dechlorinating micro-organisms, and that these HACs can enhance the extent of PCB dehalogenation in the sediments.
the enhancement in PCB dechlorinating activity was related to the number of PCB-decholorinating microorganisms and that the pattern of dechlorination varied with the structure of the HACs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HACs can be used to enhance the dechlorination of PCBs and that the extent of the enhancement is related to the population size of the PCB dechlorinating microorganism.

PCB dechlorination can be enhanced by chlorobenzenoids and chloroarenes, and that the extent of the enhancement is related to the population size of PCB-dechlorinators, and the type of chlorobenzenoid or chloroarene used.
HACs can be used as an enrichment agent for the cultivation of PCB dechlorinating microorganism.
